content.content:
use /lib
from ./project-tab import RibbonProjectTabScope
from ./code-tab import RibbonCodeTabScope
from ./spec-tab import RibbonSpecTabScope
from ./research-tab import RibbonResearchTabScope
from ./application-tab import RibbonApplicationTabScope

export scope RibbonScope:
    concept: {RibbonConcept}

concept RibbonConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the
        application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

    shape: {RibbonShape}

shape RibbonShape:
    description:
        A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab
        component with its default styling. Its tabs are, in order: Project,
        Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on
        Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups.
        There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

    openingSeveralTabs:
        Clicking a tab opens it alone, as usual. Ctrl+clicking one (Cmd+click on
        macOS) opens it alongside whichever tabs are already open, or, if it is
        already open, closes it, so any number of tabs can be open at once. The
        last open tab can't be closed this way: Ctrl+clicking it leaves it open.
        Every open tab shows as selected.

        The command area then holds the groups of every open tab side by side,
        in the order of the tabs rather than the order they were opened, with no
        divider between one tab's groups and the next, as between any groups. An
        open tab with no commands adds nothing, and "No commands yet" shows only
        when none of the open tabs has any. When the groups are wider than the
        window, the command area scrolls sideways. The command area stays the
        same height however many tabs are open.

        Double-clicking a tab still collapses the ribbon, and expanding it again
        shows the same tabs open. Which tabs are open isn't kept between
        launches: the window always opens with only Project open.

    activity:
        While anything is running, a small spinner sits just to the right of the
        project's name, as it is beside the tabs or leading the collapsed
        ribbon, with how many things are running beside it when more than one
        is. Its tooltip says what is running, or how many things are. While
        nothing is, neither shows, and nothing takes their place.

        Clicking the spinner opens a small list beneath it of everything
        running, one row each, the newest last: the task the harness is working
        on, headed "Task" with the first line of its prompt; each question still
        running, headed "Question" with its first line; a spec build,
        "Building the spec"; and a divergence analysis, "Analyzing divergence".
        Each row has a small spinner of its own. Clicking a row closes the list
        and reveals what it is: a task brings back the latest task's output,
        closing the previous tasks and any inset panel over it, and scrolls it
        to the end; a question closes the answer drawer and any inset panel, so
        its row is in view; a divergence analysis brings its panel back. A spec
        build has nothing to show, so its row only closes the list. Pressing the
        mouse outside the list, or <Escape>, closes it too, as does everything
        in it finishing.

    projectName:
        To the left of the tabs, in the same bar, sits the name of the open
        project: its folder's name, in medium weight, after a small folder
        icon, with a thin vertical divider between it and the first tab. Its
        tooltip gives the project's full path. It is only a label, and does
        nothing when clicked. While no project is open, it reads "No project",
        muted. A name wider than 320 pixels is cut off with an ellipsis.

    groups:
        Each group has its title in muted text rotated -90deg (bottom to top)
        aligned along the left edge of the group naming what its commands have
        in common. The title sits on a strip with a slightly different
        background colour, at 12px, with generous padding either side of it
        within the strip. Groups sit side by side with no divider between
        them: each group's title strip is what marks where it starts.

        A tab with no commands reads "No commands yet".

    tabs:
        Each tab is a scope of its own, which says what groups and commands it
        holds, and what each command does.

        project: @{RibbonProjectTabScope}

        code: @{RibbonCodeTabScope}

        spec: @{RibbonSpecTabScope}

        research: @{RibbonResearchTabScope}

        application: @{RibbonApplicationTabScope}

    commands:
        A command button shows a large icon above its label. An on or off
        setting, like dark mode, is a switch rather than a button.

        A command's tooltip explains what it does rather than repeating its
        label, and gives its keyboard shortcut if it has one.

        A command can be marked primary; each tab says which of its commands
        are.

        A command that can't run is disabled, not hidden, and its tooltip says
        why.

    height:
        The command area is the same height on every tab, even one with no
        commands, so the window beneath doesn't move when switching tabs.

    collapsing:
        The ribbon collapses, and expands again, with a chevron button at the
        right end of the ribbon, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1
        (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is saved for the user and
        restored on the next launch.

        Collapsed, the tabs go away too. The ribbon becomes a single thin row
        led by the project's name, as it is beside the tabs and with the same
        divider after it, and then holding every primary command, from all of
        the tabs, as small buttons: a small icon beside its label, and dark mode
        as a small switch. They keep the order of their tabs, with a thin
        vertical divider between the commands of one tab and the next, and keep
        their tooltips and disabled states. The chevron sits at the right end of
        the row. Every control in the row, the chevron and the dividers
        included, is vertically centred in it.
use /lib
from /scope/project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from /scope/new-project import NewProjectScope

export scope RibbonProjectTabScope:
    concept: {RibbonProjectTabConcept}

concept RibbonProjectTabConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon's Project tab: the commands for the project as a whole.

    shape: {RibbonProjectTabShape}

shape RibbonProjectTabShape:
    description:
        The Project tab of the ribbon, first of the tabs and the one the window
        opens on.

    groups:
        project:
            A "Project" group holds the New Project command, then the Open
            Project command.

    commands:
        newProject:
            A "New Project" button with a folder-plus icon. Clicking it opens
            the @{NewProjectScope}, and its tooltip says it creates a new
            project and opens it.

            It is primary.

        openProject:
            A button with a folder icon that always reads "Open Project…",
            whether or not a project is open; the open project's name is shown
            beside the ribbon's tabs instead. Its tooltip says to pick a
            piton.config.pi file, whose folder becomes the project.

            Clicking it opens the @{ProjectDirectoryScope} picker, and the
            folder of the file picked becomes the project. Cancelling the picker
            changes nothing, and a picker that fails shows its error as a
            notification.

            It is primary.

The loaded project indicator is now its own scope, `ProjectIndicator`, at `spec/ui/components/project-indicator/index.pi`. The code moved into its own module to match. All tests pass (169, 1 ignored).

**What the new scope covers:**
- a folder icon, then the open project's folder name in medium weight; it's only a label and does nothing when clicked;
- "No project", muted and with no tooltip, while nothing is open;
- the project's full path as its tooltip;
- names wider than 320px cut off with an ellipsis;
- it updates straight away when another project is opened or created.

**Spec changes elsewhere:**
- **Ribbon spec:** its `projectName` section is now `projectIndicator`. That section just places the indicator to the left of the tabs with a divider after it. The activity spinner and collapsed ribbon sections now say "project indicator" instead of "project's name".
- **Project tab:** the Open Project entry now points to the indicator.
- **`change-ribbon` skill:** it now refers to the indicator as a scope of its own.

**Code:** the label moved out of `src/ribbon/project_tab.rs` into the new `src/project_indicator.rs`. The ribbon calls it in the same two places as before: beside the tabs, and leading the collapsed row. Its element id is still `ribbon-project-name`, so existing tests are unchanged.

The spinner showing running tasks stays in the ribbon spec, since it's about running work rather than which project is loaded. Say if you'd like it folded into the indicator too.

`piton check`, `piton build check` and `piton build` ran cleanly, the new `ProjectIndicator.md` reference was generated, and the app builds with no warnings.
